question.text: How do changes in Wi-Fi 7/8 technology affect the measurement capability required from Oscilloscope?

messages.text: How do changes in Wi-Fi 7/8 technology affect the measurement capability required from Oscilloscope?

Wi‑Fi 8 retains Wi‑Fi 7 core PHY parameters including frequencies up to 7.125 GHz, channel bandwidth up to 320 MHz, 4096QAM, and MLO [7].
A 480 MHz WLAN waveform is described only as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn candidate waveform, not as a ratified Wi‑Fi 8 channel bandwidth [1].
Wi‑Fi 7 R&D testing requires signaling-mode RF TX/RX measurements under real-world conditions [23].
Because MLO is a key Wi‑Fi 7 feature, the supported test environment needs multiple RF chains [23].
Wi‑Fi 7-specific tests listed in the passages include 2x2 MIMO, 6 GHz out-of-band discovery, coexistence, and end-to-end test capabilities [23].
Wi‑Fi 8 shifts focus from sheer speed to ultra-high reliability performance [16].
Wi‑Fi 8 introduces testing hurdles including distributed resource units and unequal modulation [16].
dRU measurements are described as verifying uplink transmit-power boost and connection-reliability improvement [11].
UEQM analysis is described as checking whether a device adapts modulation correctly according to specified MCS combinations [11].
R&S CMX500 is supported as a multi-technology multi-channel one-box signaling tester with WLAN signaling and WLAN TX measurements covering 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, 802.11bn, and 2x2 MIMO [6].
R&S CMP180 supports bandwidths up to 500 MHz and was used to demonstrate verification of a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode [1].
